newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, March 8 Initial Claims from 307,000, March 8 4-Week Average from 310,250, March 1 Continued Claims from 2,335,000 and Feb 22 from 2,357,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 316,000 in the March 15 week.
Labor said six states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended March 8, the latest period for which data are available.
They were New York, with 5,514 fewer claims; North Carolina, with 2,968; Ohio, with 1,574; Arkansas, with 1,301; New Jersey, 1,196; and Illinois, with 1,010.

New York, Ohio and Arkansas gave no reason for the drop in claims. North Carolina reported fewer layoffs in the textile and apparel industries. New Jersey and Illinois both said they had fewer layoffs in the trade and service industries and in the manufacturing sector.
There were five states reporting increases in claims exceeding 1,000 in the March 8 week.
They were Pennsylvania, with 2,405 additional claims; Michigan, with 1,604; Kentucky, with 1,599; Tennessee, with 1,280; and Texas, with 1,266.

Pennsylvania reported layoffs in the trade and service industries while Michigan said it had layoffs in the automobile industry. Tennessee linked the increase to layoffs in the food, apparel and service industries and in agriculture. Kentucky and Texas provided no reason for their increases in claims.
